scenario: Official MCP SDK stdio client reads fixture, denied write preserves SHA-256, policy override permits write, fixture restored; React displays actual events.

commands.cmd: npm run build (initial SDK signature error; corrected)
npm run e2e (initial missing browser / FFmpeg; resolved)
npm run browsers:install (optional full-browser download stopped; cached executable used)
npm run e2e (PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE_PATH set to existing compatible Chromium)
npm run demo (PLAYWRIGHT_EXECUTABLE_PATH set to existing compatible Chromium)

limitations: Controlled two-tool gateway, not a universal MCP interceptor.
No inference: real deterministic enforcement on explicitly labelled fixture data.
Single-operator mutable audit; last 100 events; no cross-process locking or tamper resistance.

Browser verification reused an existing Chromium executable read-only and downloaded matching FFmpeg into project cache. Fresh-clone headless browser installation was not verified; an earlier slow full-browser download was stopped.
No OS sandbox or authentication; hostile local processes and filesystem races are out of scope.
